text: Requirements are signed off. Before a single server gets racked, this video draws a hard line around what phase one of Brennan Manufacturing's engagement actually delivers.

V1 ships the relational foundation: BrennanWSFC and BrennanAG with BrennanERP protected from day one, a proven performance baseline, and dbatools automation so backups and maintenance don't depend on anyone remembering.

A product team already stood up a MongoDB database, brennan-mongo-01, with zero DBA oversight -- no confirmed backup, no access review. That's real risk, scoped honestly as Phase 2 of this same engagement, not a separate someday project.
When Dana asks for a quick look at Mongo right now, the answer isn't no -- it's that the database deserves its own focused phase, right after the cluster that actually halts production is proven.
Scope is locked and signed. Next: the real architecture decision -- why an Availability Group, not just nightly backups.
